entries.reason: DecodeStage remains the Fovea host owner of probe revalidation, codec capability negotiation, generic-plus-backend working-set admission, prepared-state lifecycle, blocking execution, cancellation and aggregate diagnostics. Swift 6.4 async defer now makes subscription release, preparation discard and priority-control completion structurally unavoidable without adding mutable state or a new responsibility. These operations still form one permit, prepared-state and failure transaction; splitting before a second production backend demonstrates a stable collaborator would duplicate admission ordering, cancellation mapping or prepared-state cleanup.
responsibilities: host-owned bounded probe validation and preparation
public codec capability and conservative resource admission
decode executor, permit and prepared-state lifecycle
aggregate diagnostics, failure mapping and cancellation
splitTriggers: a stable responsibility can move without sharing mutable state or transaction ordering

entries.reason: SharedTaskRegistry is one actor state machine covering subscription cohorts, effective priority, completion visibility, orphan handoff leases and cancellation tombstones. Completed entries remain joinable only inside the active cohort and can be explicitly invalidated before a fresh cache-observation transaction. Absolute monotonic expiry and lazy admission checks make timers cleanup optimizations rather than correctness dependencies. Keeping entry, invalidation, tombstone, lease identity, completion and join transitions in one actor preserves the linearization boundary and prevents ABA races.
responsibilities: absolute cancellation tombstone admission and retention

modules.reason: FoveaCore remains the Fovea-owned policy and orchestration layer for request identity, geometry, resource admission, fetch/decode execution, namespace lifecycle, shared work and diagnostics. PipelineCache was split into four files after its frozen oversized-file review triggered, reducing local review scope without changing the module boundary. The cache base, rendered aliases, transport-verified handoffs and original-publication transaction still share FoveaCore identities, namespace authority, diagnostics and mutation ordering; extracting them would either import FoveaCore back into the new module or duplicate host-owned authority. The 57-file set preserves one-way package dependencies and remains below the reviewed 0.60 source-share ceiling.
responsibilities: cache, transient handoff and namespace transaction coordination
codec host conformance, shared-work lifecycle and diagnostics
splitTriggers: source share exceeds the reviewed 0.60 ceiling
a stable policy family can move without importing FoveaCore back into the new module
